sanskrit: kiṃ te dhanair bāndhavair vāpi kiṃ te; kiṃ te dārair brāhmaṇa yo mariṣyasi ātmānam anviccha guhāṃ praviṣṭaṃ; pitāmahas te kva gataḥ pitā ca
english: What use to you are riches, what use your kinsmen? What use to you a wife, O brāhmaṇa, you who must die? Seek out the Self that has entered the cave of the heart. Where has your grandfather gone, and where your father?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca putrasyaitad vacaḥ śrutvā tathākārṣīt pitā nṛpa tathā tvam api vartasva satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having heard these words of his son, the father did accordingly, O king. So should you too conduct yourself, devoted wholly to truth and dharma.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dhanino vādhanā ye ca vartayanti svatantriṇaḥ sukhaduḥkhāgamas teṣāṃ kaḥ kathaṃ vā pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Those who live as their own masters, whether rich or poor — how does happiness and sorrow come upon them, and in what manner, O grandfather?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam śamyākena vimuktena gītaṃ śāntigatena ha
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recite an ancient tale — what was sung by Śamyāka, a man set free, who had attained tranquillity.

sanskrit: abravīn māṃ purā kaś cid brāhmaṇas tyāgam āsthitaḥ kliśyamānaḥ kudāreṇa kucailena bubhukṣayā
english: A certain brāhmaṇa, established in renunciation, once spoke to me — a man afflicted by a poor wife, by ragged clothing, and by hunger.

sanskrit: utpannam iha loke vai janmaprabhṛti mānavam vividhāny upavartante duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca
english: Once a man is born into this world, from the very moment of birth manifold sorrows and joys come crowding upon him.

sanskrit: tayor ekatare mārge yady enam abhisaṃnayet na sukhaṃ prāpya saṃhṛṣyen na duḥkhaṃ prāpya saṃjvaret
english: If either of these two should lead him onto its road, let him not exult on gaining happiness, nor burn with anguish on meeting sorrow.

sanskrit: na vai carasi yac chreya ātmano vā yad īhase akāmātmāpi hi sadā dhuram udyamya caiva hi
english: You do not pursue what is truly best for the Self, nor what you strive after; yet even desireless you forever take up the yoke and bear it.

sanskrit: akiṃcanaḥ paripatan sukham āsvādayiṣyasi akiṃcanaḥ sukhaṃ śete samuttiṣṭhati caiva hi
english: Owning nothing, wandering free, you shall taste happiness; the man who owns nothing sleeps in peace and rises in peace as well.

sanskrit: ākiṃcanyaṃ sukhaṃ loke pathyaṃ śivam anāmayam anamitram atho hy etad durlabhaṃ sulabhaṃ satām
english: Possessionlessness is happiness in this world — wholesome, blessed, free of disease, and free of enemies; hard for most to win, yet easily won by the good.

sanskrit: akiṃcanasya śuddhasya upapannasya sarvaśaḥ avekṣamāṇas trīṃl lokān na tulyam upalakṣaye
english: Surveying the three worlds, I see nothing to equal the man who owns nothing, who is pure and complete in every way.

sanskrit: ākiṃcanyaṃ ca rājyaṃ ca tulayā samatolayam atyaricyata dāridryaṃ rājyād api guṇādhikam
english: I weighed possessionlessness and kingship together in the balance, and poverty outweighed kingship, richer still in virtue.

sanskrit: ākiṃcanye ca rājye ca viśeṣaḥ sumahān ayam nityodvigno hi dhanavān mṛtyor āsyagato yathā
english: Between possessionlessness and kingship the difference is vast indeed: the wealthy man is forever in dread, like one held in the very jaws of death.

sanskrit: naivāsyāgnir na cādityo na mṛtyur na ca dasyavaḥ prabhavanti dhanajyāninirmuktasya nirāśiṣaḥ
english: Neither fire nor the sun, neither death nor robbers can prevail against the man who is free of the ruin that wealth brings and free of all craving.

sanskrit: taṃ vai sadā kāmacaram anupastīrṇaśāyinam bāhūpadhānaṃ śāmyantaṃ praśaṃsanti divaukasaḥ
english: Him the dwellers in heaven ever praise — the man who roams at will, who lies down on no spread bed, his arm for a pillow, abiding in stillness.

sanskrit: dhanavān krodhalobhābhyām āviṣṭo naṣṭacetanaḥ tiryagīkṣaḥ śuṣkamukhaḥ pāpako bhrukuṭīmukhaḥ
english: The wealthy man, possessed by anger and greed, his wits undone, looks askance with a dry mouth, malign, his face contorted in a scowl.

sanskrit: nirdaśaṃś cādharoṣṭhaṃ ca kruddho dāruṇabhāṣitā kas tam icchet paridraṣṭuṃ dātum icchati cen mahīm
english: Biting his lower lip in his rage, harsh in his speech — who would wish even to look upon such a man, though he offered to grant the whole earth?

sanskrit: śriyā hy abhīkṣṇaṃ saṃvāso mohayaty avicakṣaṇam sā tasya cittaṃ harati śāradābhram ivānilaḥ
english: Constant fellowship with Fortune deludes the man without discernment; she carries off his mind as the wind sweeps away an autumn cloud.

sanskrit: athainaṃ rūpamānaś ca dhanamānaś ca vindati abhijāto 'smi siddho 'smi nāsmi kevalamānuṣaḥ ity ebhiḥ kāraṇais tasya tribhiś cittaṃ prasicyate
english: Then pride of beauty and pride of wealth take hold of him: "I am nobly born, I am accomplished, I am no mere mortal" — by these three causes his mind is overflowed and swept away.

sanskrit: sa prasiktamanā bhogān visṛjya pitṛsaṃcitān parikṣīṇaḥ parasvānām ādānaṃ sādhu manyate
english: His mind thus carried off, he squanders the enjoyments his fathers had heaped up, and once reduced to want, he thinks it fitting to seize the goods of others.

sanskrit: tam atikrāntamaryādam ādadānaṃ tatas tataḥ pratiṣedhanti rājāno lubdhā mṛgam iveṣubhiḥ
english: As he oversteps all bounds, snatching from this side and that, the kings hold him back, the greedy man, as huntsmen check a beast with their arrows.

sanskrit: evam etāni duḥkhāni tāni tānīha mānavam vividhāny upavartante gātrasaṃsparśajāni ca
english: Thus do these sorrows, and those, of many kinds, come upon a man in this life, and with them too the pains born of the body's contact with things.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ paramaduḥkhānāṃ buddhyā bhaiṣajyam ācaret lokadharmaṃ samājñāya dhruvāṇām adhruvaiḥ saha
english: For those supreme sorrows let a man apply the remedy of wisdom, having well understood the way of the world — that the lasting goes mingled with the fleeting.

sanskrit: nātyaktvā sukham āpnoti nātyaktvā vindate param nātyaktvā cābhayaḥ śete tyaktvā sarvaṃ sukhī bhava
english: Without renouncing, one wins no happiness; without renouncing, one attains not the highest; without renouncing, one sleeps not free of fear — so renounce all and be happy.

sanskrit: ity etad dhāstinapure brāhmaṇenopavarṇitam śamyākena purā mahyaṃ tasmāt tyāgaḥ paro mataḥ
english: Thus was this set forth to me long ago in Hāstinapura by the brāhmaṇa Śamyāka; and therefore renunciation is held by me to be supreme.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca īhamānaḥ samārambhān yadi nāsādayed dhanam dhanatṛṣṇābhibhūtaś ca kiṃ kurvan sukham āpnuyāt
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: If a man, straining at his ventures, fails to gain wealth, and is overborne by the thirst for wealth — by what conduct might he yet find happiness?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sarvasāmyam anāyāsaḥ satyavākyaṃ ca bhārata nirvedaś cāvivitsā ca yasya syāt sa sukhī naraḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Even-mindedness toward all, freedom from striving, truthful speech, O Bhārata, dispassion and the absence of craving to know — the man who has these is the happy one.

sanskrit: etāny eva padāny āhuḥ pañca vṛddhāḥ praśāntaye eṣa svargaś ca dharmaś ca sukhaṃ cānuttamaṃ satām
english: These five steps, the elders say, lead to tranquillity; and this is heaven, this is dharma, and this the unsurpassed happiness of the good.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nirvedān maṅkinā gītaṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this too they recite an ancient tale — what Maṅki sang out of his dispassion; hear it now, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: īhamāno dhanaṃ maṅkir bhagnehaś ca punaḥ punaḥ kena cid dhanaśeṣeṇa krītavān damyagoyugam
english: Maṅki, striving after wealth, his efforts broken again and again, with the last remnant of his money bought a pair of young oxen for the yoke.

sanskrit: susaṃbaddhau tu tau damyau damanāyābhiniḥsṛtau āsīnam uṣṭraṃ madhyena sahasaivābhyadhāvatām
english: The two untrained beasts, well harnessed, set out to be broken in, and all at once they rushed straight past a camel that sat in their path.

sanskrit: tayoḥ saṃprāptayor uṣṭraḥ skandhadeśam amarṣaṇaḥ utthāyotkṣipya tau damyau prasasāra mahājavaḥ
english: As the two reached its shoulders, the camel, enraged, sprang up, hoisted the pair of young oxen aloft, and bolted away at great speed.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇau tu tau damyau tenoṣṭreṇa pramāthinā mriyamāṇau ca saṃprekṣya maṅkis tatrābravīd idam
english: Seeing his two young oxen carried off by that furious camel, and dying as they were carried, Maṅki spoke these words then and there:

sanskrit: na caivāvihitaṃ śakyaṃ dakṣeṇāpīhituṃ dhanam yuktena śraddhayā samyag īhāṃ samanutiṣṭhatā
english: Wealth that fate has not ordained cannot be won even by the able man — even by one diligent, full of faith, pursuing his effort rightly.

sanskrit: kṛtasya pūrvaṃ cānarthair yuktasyāpy anutiṣṭhataḥ imaṃ paśyata saṃgatyā mama daivam upaplavam
english: Though I labored beforehand, beset by misfortunes, and toiled on still, behold by what chance my fate has overtaken me with calamity!

sanskrit: udyamyodyamya me damyau viṣameṇeva gacchati utkṣipya kākatālīyam unmātheneva jambukaḥ
english: Heaving up my two young beasts again and again, it makes off as over rough ground, tossing them by sheer chance — as a jackal is crushed by a falling palm-fruit.

sanskrit: maṇī voṣṭrasya lambete priyau vatsatarau mama śuddhaṃ hi daivam evedam ato naivāsti pauruṣam
english: My two dear young bullocks dangle like the two pendants at a camel's neck. This is fate, pure and simple; here there is no human effort at all.

sanskrit: yadi vāpy upapadyeta pauruṣaṃ nāma karhi cit anviṣyamāṇaṃ tad api daivam evāvatiṣṭhate
english: And even if what is called human effort should somewhere come to bear, when one searches it out, that too rests upon fate alone.

sanskrit: tasmān nirveda eveha gantavyaḥ sukham īpsatā sukhaṃ svapiti nirviṇṇo nirāśaś cārthasādhane
english: Therefore the man who longs for happiness must come to dispassion in this world; the dispassionate sleeps in peace, having given up hope of gaining gain.

sanskrit: aho samyak śukenoktaṃ sarvataḥ parimucyatā pratiṣṭhatā mahāraṇyaṃ janakasya niveśanāt
english: Ah, how rightly it was spoken by Śuka, who set himself free from everything, departing from Janaka's dwelling into the great forest!

sanskrit: yaḥ kāmān prāpnuyāt sarvān yaś cainān kevalāṃs tyajet prāpaṇāt sarvakāmānāṃ parityāgo viśiṣyate
english: Of him who might obtain all desires and him who would utterly renounce them, the renunciation of all desires surpasses the gaining of them all.

sanskrit: nāntaṃ sarvavivitsānāṃ gatapūrvo 'sti kaś cana śarīre jīvite caiva tṛṣṇā mandasya vardhate
english: No one has ever yet reached the end of all his cravings to know; for the dull-witted man, thirst only swells — thirst for the body and for life itself.

sanskrit: nivartasva vivitsābhyaḥ śāmya nirvidya māmaka asakṛc cāsi nikṛto na ca nirvidyase tano
english: Turn back, O my own self, from your cravings to know; grow calm, grow weary of them. Time and again you have been thwarted, and still, my dear body, you take no disgust at it.

sanskrit: yadi nāhaṃ vināśyas te yady evaṃ ramase mayā mā māṃ yojaya lobhena vṛthā tvaṃ vittakāmuka
english: If I am not to be your ruin, if you would still take your delight in me, then do not yoke me to greed in vain, you craver of riches!

sanskrit: saṃcitaṃ saṃcitaṃ dravyaṃ naṣṭaṃ tava punaḥ punaḥ kadā vimokṣyase mūḍha dhanehāṃ dhanakāmuka
english: Heaped up and heaped up, your goods have been lost again and again. When will you let go, you fool, your longing for wealth, you craver of wealth?

sanskrit: aho nu mama bāliśyaṃ yo 'haṃ krīḍanakas tava kiṃ naiva jātu puruṣaḥ pareṣāṃ preṣyatām iyāt
english: Ah, what folly is mine, that I have been your plaything! Should a man ever sink into bondage as the servant of others?

sanskrit: na pūrve nāpare jātu kāmānām antam āpnuvan tyaktvā sarvasamārambhān pratibuddho 'smi jāgṛmi
english: Neither those of old nor those of later times have ever reached the end of desires. Forsaking all my ventures, I am awakened now — I am awake!

sanskrit: nūnaṃ te hṛdayaṃ kāma vajrasāramayaṃ dṛdham yad anarthaśatāviṣṭaṃ śatadhā na vidīryate
english: Surely your heart, O Desire, is hard and made of the very essence of adamant, that, beset by a hundred miseries, it is not split into a hundred shards.

sanskrit: tyajāmi kāma tvāṃ caiva yac ca kiṃ cit priyaṃ tava tavāhaṃ sukham anvicchann ātmany upalabhe sukham
english: I renounce you, Desire, and all that is dear to you. Seeking your happiness, I now find happiness instead within my own Self.

sanskrit: kāma jānāmi te mūlaṃ saṃkalpāt kila jāyase na tvāṃ saṃkalpayiṣyāmi samūlo na bhaviṣyasi
english: Desire, I know your root: it is from willful imagining that you are born. I shall imagine you no longer, and so, root and all, you shall cease to be.

sanskrit: īhā dhanasya na sukhā labdhvā cintā ca bhūyasī labdhanāśo yathā mṛtyur labdhaṃ bhavati vā na vā
english: The striving for wealth is no happiness; once gained, the anxiety only grows. To lose what is gained is like death, and whether it stays gained or not remains uncertain.

sanskrit: paretya yo na labhate tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim na ca tuṣyati labdhena bhūya eva ca mārgati
english: For him who exerts himself and gains nothing — what is more painful than that? And he who gains is not content with what he has gained, but only seeks for more.

sanskrit: anutarṣula evārthaḥ svādu gāṅgam ivodakam madvilāpanam etat tu pratibuddho 'smi saṃtyaja
english: Wealth only breeds fresh thirst, sweet as the water of the Gaṅgā; yet this is what undoes me. I am awakened now — let it go!

sanskrit: ya imaṃ māmakaṃ dehaṃ bhūtagrāmaḥ samāśritaḥ sa yātv ito yathākāmaṃ vasatāṃ vā yathāsukham
english: Whatever throng of elements has taken shelter in this body of mine — let it depart hence as it pleases, or dwell on as it finds ease.

sanskrit: na yuṣmāsv iha me prītiḥ kāmalobhānusāriṣu tasmād utsṛjya sarvān vaḥ satyam evāśrayāmy aham
english: I take no delight in you here, you that run after desire and greed; therefore, casting you all off, I take refuge in truth alone.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtāny ahaṃ dehe paśyan manasi cātmanaḥ yoge buddhiṃ śrute sattvaṃ mano brahmaṇi dhārayan
english: Beholding all beings within my body and within the mind of the Self, fixing my intellect on yoga, my being on sacred lore, and my mind on Brahman —

sanskrit: vihariṣyāmy anāsaktaḥ sukhī lokān nirāmayaḥ yathā mā tvaṃ punar naivaṃ duḥkheṣu praṇidhāsyasi
english: I shall wander free of attachment, happy and untroubled through the worlds, so that you, Desire, may never again plunge me thus into sorrows.

sanskrit: tvayā hi me praṇunnasya gatir anyā na vidyate tṛṣṇāśokaśramāṇāṃ hi tvaṃ kāma prabhavaḥ sadā
english: For driven on by you, I find no other course; for you, O Desire, are forever the wellspring of thirst, of grief, and of toil.

sanskrit: dhananāśo 'dhikaṃ duḥkhaṃ manye sarvamahattaram jñātayo hy avamanyante mitrāṇi ca dhanacyutam
english: The loss of wealth I count the greater grief, greatest of all; for kinsmen and friends alike despise the man fallen from his riches.

sanskrit: avajñānasahasrais tu doṣāḥ kaṣṭatarādhane dhane sukhakalā yā ca sāpi duḥkhair vidhīyate
english: In poverty the troubles are harsher, with a thousand humiliations; and what little fraction of happiness lies in wealth, that too is meted out only through sorrows.

sanskrit: dhanam asyeti puruṣaṃ purā nighnanti dasyavaḥ kliśyanti vividhair daṇḍair nityam udvejayanti ca
english: "This man has wealth" — and at once robbers strike him down, torment him with manifold punishments, and harry him without end.

sanskrit: mandalolupatā duḥkham iti buddhaṃ cirān mayā yad yad ālambase kāma tat tad evānurudhyase
english: That the dull man's covetousness is misery I have understood at long last: whatever you fasten upon, O Desire, to that very thing you bind yourself.

sanskrit: atattvajño 'si bālaś ca dustoṣo 'pūraṇo 'nalaḥ naiva tvaṃ vettha sulabhaṃ naiva tvaṃ vettha durlabham
english: You know not the truth of things, you are a child, hard to satisfy, a fire never to be filled. You know not what is easy to win, nor what is hard.

sanskrit: pātālam iva duṣpūro māṃ duḥkhair yoktum icchasi nāham adya samāveṣṭuṃ śakyaḥ kāma punas tvayā
english: Hard to fill as the netherworld, you wish to yoke me to sorrows; but no longer, Desire, can you wrap me round again.

sanskrit: nirvedam aham āsādya dravyanāśād yadṛcchayā nirvṛtiṃ paramāṃ prāpya nādya kāmān vicintaye
english: Having come, by the chance loss of my goods, to dispassion, and having reached the highest peace, I no longer give a thought to desires.

sanskrit: atikleśān sahāmīha nāhaṃ budhyāmy abuddhimān nikṛto dhananāśena śaye sarvāṅgavijvaraḥ
english: I have borne extreme afflictions here, witless and unawakened; brought low by the loss of wealth, I lay with every limb burning with fever.

sanskrit: parityajāmi kāma tvāṃ hitvā sarvamanogatīḥ na tvaṃ mayā punaḥ kāma nasyoteneva raṃsyase
english: I cast you off entirely, O Desire, abandoning every wandering of the mind. No more, Desire, will you make sport with me as with a beast led by a nose-rope.

sanskrit: kṣamiṣye 'kṣamamāṇānāṃ na hiṃsiṣye ca hiṃsitaḥ dveṣyamuktaḥ priyaṃ vakṣyāmy anādṛtya tad apriyam
english: I shall forgive those who do not forgive; though injured, I shall do no injury; spoken to with hatred, I shall answer kindly, paying no heed to that unkindness.

sanskrit: tṛptaḥ svasthendriyo nityaṃ yathālabdhena vartayan na sakāmaṃ kariṣyāmi tvām ahaṃ śatrum ātmanaḥ
english: Content, my senses ever at rest within themselves, living on whatever comes to hand, I will not let you have your way, you who are the enemy of my Self.

sanskrit: nirvedaṃ nirvṛtiṃ tṛptiṃ śāntiṃ satyaṃ damaṃ kṣamām sarvabhūtadayāṃ caiva viddhi māṃ śaraṇāgatam
english: Know that I have taken refuge in dispassion, in repose, in contentment, in peace, in truth, in self-restraint, in forbearance, and in compassion for all beings.

sanskrit: tasmāt kāmaś ca lobhaś ca tṛṣṇā kārpaṇyam eva ca tyajantu māṃ pratiṣṭhantaṃ sattvastho hy asmi sāṃpratam
english: Therefore let desire and greed, thirst and wretchedness, all forsake me as I take my stand; for now I am established in pure being.

sanskrit: prahāya kāmaṃ lobhaṃ ca krodhaṃ pāruṣyam eva ca nādya lobhavaśaṃ prāpto duḥkhaṃ prāpsyāmy anātmavān
english: Having cast away desire and greed, anger and harshness, no longer fallen under the sway of greed shall I, an undisciplined man, come to grief.

sanskrit: yad yat tyajati kāmānāṃ tat sukhasyābhipūryate kāmasya vaśago nityaṃ duḥkham eva prapadyate
english: Each desire that a man renounces, by just so much is he filled with happiness; but he who is forever in thrall to desire walks straight into sorrow.

sanskrit: kāmān vyudasya dhunute yat kiṃ cit puruṣo rajaḥ kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ duḥkham ahrīr aratir eva ca
english: Casting aside desires, a man shakes off whatever passion clings to him — the sorrow born of desire and anger, and shamelessness, and discontent as well.

sanskrit: eṣa brahmapraviṣṭo 'haṃ grīṣme śītam iva hradam śāmyāmi parinirvāmi sukham āse ca kevalam
english: Here am I, entered into Brahman as into a cool lake in the heat of summer; I grow still, I am wholly quenched, and I abide in pure happiness alone.

sanskrit: yac ca kāmasukhaṃ loke yac ca divyaṃ mahat sukham tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ kalām
english: Whatever happiness of desire there is in the world, and whatever great happiness is divine — these are not worth a sixteenth part of the happiness that is the extinction of thirst.

sanskrit: ātmanā saptamaṃ kāmaṃ hatvā śatrum ivottamam prāpyāvadhyaṃ brahmapuraṃ rājeva syām ahaṃ sukhī
english: Having slain Desire — the seventh enemy, counting the Self — as one slays a foremost foe, and reached the unassailable city of Brahman, I shall be happy as a king.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthāya maṅkir nirvedam āgataḥ sarvān kāmān parityajya prāpya brahma mahat sukham
english: Taking his stand upon this insight, Maṅki came to dispassion, and forsaking all desires, attained Brahman, the great happiness.

sanskrit: damyanāśakṛte maṅkir amaratvaṃ kilāgamat acchinat kāmamūlaṃ sa tena prāpa mahat sukham
english: Through the loss of his young oxen, it is said, Maṅki attained immortality; he cut away the root of desire, and thereby won the great happiness.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gītaṃ videharājena janakena praśāmyatā
english: On this too they recite an ancient tale — what was sung by Janaka, king of the Videhas, as he attained tranquillity.
